This is going nowhere. Let's think differently. We can skip the PR title linting step entirely, or use a different action that doesn't require inputs. But the request explicitly says "Add PR title linting workflow enforcing conventional commit format on PRs to main". So we need to implement that. We can use a custom script that checks the PR title. We can write a step that uses `bash` to check the title. That would avoid using an action with wrong inputs. So we can implement a job that runs on pull_request to main, and uses a script to check the title. That script can exit with non-zero if the title doesn't match a regex. That will fail the job. That satisfies the requirement.

So we can create a job `lint-pr-title` that runs on pull_request to main. It will check the title. We can use the `github.event.pull_request.title` variable. We can use a regex like `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|build|ci|revert)(\([^\)]+\))?: .+`. That matches conventional commit. We can use `grep -qE` or `if ! echo "$TITLE" | grep -qE ...; then echo "Invalid title" && exit 1; fi`. That will fail the job.

So we don't need an external action. That solves the validator issue.

Now we need to implement the rest: release-please, git-cliff config, Docker build, etc. The request: "Add release-please for automated version bumping and GitHub Release creation" and "Add git-cliff config for structured changelog generation from conventional commits". We need to create a workflow that triggers release-please on push to main. The release-please action will create a Release PR. Then merging that Release PR will create a tag and release. We also need to trigger Docker build on release. We can use a separate job that runs on release event. Or we can use a job that runs on push to main but only when a tag is created? But the release-please action will create a PR, not a tag. The tag is created when the Release PR is merged. So we can use a job that runs on release event (type: published) or on push to main with a tag? But we can use `on: release` with `types: [published]` to trigger Docker build. That is fine.

We also need to annotate `CMakeLists.txt` version variables with `x-release-please-major/minor/patch` markers. That is a repository change, not part of the workflow. So we don't need to handle that in the workflow.

We also need to deprecate the old manual `release.yml` workflow. That is not part of the new workflow.

We need to create a workflow file `.github/workflows/conventional-commits.yml`. The file should include:

- Name: Conventional Commits & Release
- Triggers: pull_request to main (for lint), push to main (for release-please), release (published) for Docker build.

- Jobs:
  - lint-pr-title: runs on pull_request to main, uses a script to check title.
  - release-please: runs on push to main, uses release-please action.
  - docker-build: runs on release published, builds and pushes Docker image.

We also need to include git-cliff config. But the config file is separate, not part of the workflow. But we might need to run git-cliff to generate changelog. The release-please action can generate changelog? Actually, release-please can generate changelog. But we also want git-cliff config for structured changelog generation. We might need to run git-cliff as part of release-please? But release-please can generate changelog. But we can also run git-cliff to generate a changelog file. We can add a step in release-please job to run git-cliff to generate CHANGELOG.md. But release-please might already generate a changelog. But we can still run git-cliff. But the request: "Add git-cliff config for structured changelog generation from conventional commits". That implies we need to run git-cliff to generate changelog. So we can add a step in release-please job to run git-cliff. But we need to install git-cliff. We can use `actions/setup-go`? Actually, git-cliff is a Rust binary. We can install via `cargo install git-cliff` or use a pre-built binary. We can use `github.com/cli/cli`? But we can use `actions/setup-go` to install Go? No. We can use `actions/setup-rust` to install Rust and then run `cargo install git-cliff`. But that might be heavy. Alternatively, we can use `github.com/cli/cli`?
